data.name: Omkara
data.gender_notes: Omkara is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Omkara is the supreme syllable OM, representing the ultimate reality and the universe's essence in Hinduism. The name Omkara carries the meaning “Supreme syllable OM” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Omkara usually hope their child will grow to embody supreme syllable om and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Omkara total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Omkara holds great cultural significance in Hinduism, representing the primordial sounds or the creation mantra. It is believed that reciting or hearing the word "Om" can bring about a sense of inner peace and spiritual growth. In Hindu temples and spiritual practices, the syllable "Om" is often used to begin and end prayers or rituals.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Omkara is considered the universal sound or the divine cosmic vibration. It is the symbol of the three major Hindu gods: Brahma (creation), Vishnu (preservation), and Shiva (destroyer). Chanting or hearing Omkara is believed to connect an individual to the divine and create a deep sense of spiritual awareness. In Hindu philosophy, Omkara is believed to be beyond the limitations of time, space, and language, transcending all dualities and bringing about unity and oneness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Omkara is a sacred syllable in Hinduism, symbolizing the ultimate reality and the sound of the universe. It represents the cosmic vibration of creation and signifies the union of Atman (soul) with Brahman (supreme consciousness).
